source.stem:
A ball is dropped from a table-top. Air resistance may be ignored.
Which row describes the velocity and the acceleration of the ball at point X?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: atmosphere is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: A pressure difference across the object is needed for a net push.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: The cause and effect in this law run in the opposite direction.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when A pressure difference across the object is needed for a net push is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Atmospheric air surrounds the Earth and exerts pressure; when air pressure is lower inside a sealed space than outside, the higher outside pressure pushes the object against the surface. Removing air from one side lowers pressure there, so the greater atmospheric pressure on the other side produces a net push; a larger exposed area gives air pressure a larger total force. The learner explains atmospheric-pressure effects through outside air pressure over an area and pressure differences across an object. Air is too light to press strongly, so a rubber sucker sticks mainly because rubber is sticky.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Pressure. The student must decide: Decide when an effect is caused by atmospheric pressure acting over an area or by a pressure difference across an object.
